sv:agera.etymology: agō, from *h₂éǵeti. Cognate with agere, also a Latin borrowing. Compare also åka, which derives from aka, from the same ultimate Proto-Indo-European verb.

sv:aktuell.etymology: From actuel, perhaps via aktuell, from actuālis, from āctus + -ālis.

sv:aldrig.etymology: From aldri, aldrigi. Cognate with aldrei, aldri, aldri and aldrig.

sv:all.etymology: From alder, from allr, from *allaz, from *h₂el-.

sv:allra.etymology: From aldra, the genitive plural of all, from allr. Originally "of all" or "among all".

sv:alls.etymology: From alz, influenced by Low German alles.

sv:alltid.etymology: From tid, literally "all time". Compare altid, altijd, ætíð, alltid, alltid.

sv:alltså.etymology: Borrowed from also. Compare allt and så. Cognate to altså and altso.

sv:allvar.etymology: From alvara, from an adjective ǫlværr, maybe from alwār.

sv:an.etymology: Borrowed from an and an, and less commonly from on, from *ana, cognate with on and doublet of å, på.

sv:annorlunda.etymology: From annorlund, annerlunda, anner lundh or lunda

sv:anse.etymology: From anse, from ansen. Equivalent to se.

sv:anställa.etymology: From anstellen, equivalent to ställa. Compare aanstellen.

sv:anta.etymology: antaga, calqued from annemen or annehmen. All compounds with the verb ta have gone through apocope and those forms are now the standard ones, see also avta/avtaga, inta/intaga and överta/övertaga. Cognate with antage, an

sv:antagligen.etymology: en. Compare and antagelig, whence also antakeleg.

sv:aptit.etymology: Appetit, from appétit, from appetītus, from -tus. Compare appetit, appetite.

sv:arbeta.etymology: From arbeida, arbeta, from arbeiden, from arvēdian, from *arbaidijaną, from *arbaidiz, equivalent of a. Compare arbeide, arbeide, arbeida, arbejde, arabeitjan, arabeiton, arbeiten and 𐌰𐍂𐌱𐌰𐌹𐌳𐌾𐌰𐌽.

sv:arg.etymology: From argher, from argr, from *argaz, from *h₃orǵʰ-, *h₃erǵʰ-.

sv:autentisk.etymology: Cognate with authentisch, authentic and authentical, authentique, from authenticus and αὐθεντικός, used in Swedish since 1755.

sv:avgå.etymology: From gå, like abgehen, go off.

sv:avsluta.etymology: From sluta. Compare to avslutta and afslutte

sv:bak.etymology: From baker, from bak, from *baką. Related to back.

sv:bara.etymology: From bara, from *bara, from *barr, from *bazaz. Compare bara.

sv:bedriva.etymology: From bedriva, from bedrîven. Equivalent to driva. Cognate with bedrive, bedrive, betreiben, bedrijven and bedrive.

sv:befinna.etymology: From bevinden, from bifindan. Equivalent to finna. Cognate with befinne, befinde, befinden, bevinden, befind and befiende.

sv:befria.etymology: From bevrien and befreien. Cognate with befri, befri, באַפֿרײַען, bevrien, older bevrijen, now bevrijden, befrije, befrēoġan, *befreen, *bifreen and befree. Equivalent to -a or fria.

sv:begränsa.etymology: From begrenzen, equivalent to -a or gränsa. Cognate with begrænse, begrense, begrenzen and begrenzen, beschränken.saob

sv:begå.etymology: From bega, from began. Equivalent to gå.

sv:behov.etymology: behof, borrowed from behof, from *bihōf, from *bihōf.

sv:behålla.etymology: From behalda, beholda, from beholden, from bihaldan.

sv:behöva.etymology: a, cognate with behoove (US) / behove (UK) and behoeven.

sv:bekräfta.etymology: From bekreften or bekräften (rare, more often bekräftigen), from bekreften. Equivalent of -a. The synonym bekräftiga went out of use during the 17th century. Cognate with bekræfte, bekrefte and bekrefte, bekrefta.

sv:bekväm.etymology: From beqvæmber. Compare bequem, bekwaam, bekvem.

sv:bekymra.etymology: bekymbra, from bekummeren, bekumberen. For the second element see Kummer. Cognate of bekommeren, bekümmern.

sv:belasta.etymology: From belasten. Equivalent to lasta. Cognate with belaste and belasten.

sv:belöna.etymology: From belonen or belohnen, equivalent to löna. Cognate with belønne, belønne, belonen, beloon, beloene, beleanje, beloonje, belounen and באַלוינען.

sv:bero.etymology: From beruhen (older form also berugen) or - *berouwen, equivalent to ro. Cognate with bero and bero.

sv:berätta.etymology: From berætta, from berichten, in correspondence to rätta (verb) and rätt (verb and noun), equivalent to -a or rätta. Cognate with berette, berette, berichten, berechten, bericht, berig, berichten, Bericht and beriichten.

sv:beröra.etymology: From beroren, from beroren, ultimately from *bi-, *hrōzijaną, equivalent to röra. Cognate with berøre, berøre, berühren and beroeren.

sv:besked.etymology: From beskedh, from besched, from bescheden.

sv:beslut.etymology: From beslut, from beslut, a besluten. 1513. Compare besluit, Beschluss.

sv:beställa.etymology: From bestellen or a Low German equivalent. ställa.

sv:besvärlig.etymology: From beschwerlich, equivalent to lig. Cognate with besværlig, besværlig and bezwaarlijk.

sv:besöka.etymology: From besøkia, from besoken, equivalent to söka. Cognate with besøge, besøke, besøke, besøka, besøkje, besøkja, bezoeken, besuchen, besäike, beseech, beseek and beseik.

sv:betala.etymology: From betala, bitala, bittala, from betalen, equivalent to tala.saob Cognate with betale, betale, betala, betale, betalen, betelje, bezahlen, betahlen and betall. Displaced native gälda.

sv:betrakta.etymology: betrachten. Equivalent to trakta. Attested since the 14th century.

sv:betyda.etymology: From bethydha, from beduden, equivalent to tyda.saob Cognate with betyde, bety, bety, bedeuten, bydȧjta, bedeiten, beduiden, older bedieden, beduuje, betjuude and betsjutte.

sv:bild.etymology: From Bild, from bilde, from biladi, bilidi. beläte.

sv:bill.etymology: From bilder, from bíldr, from *bīþlaz. An instrumental derivation of *bītaną. Closely related to bila.

sv:billig.etymology: From billik, billich. Compare billig and billijk.

sv:bli.etymology: bliva, from bliva, from blîven, from bilīvan, from *bilīban, from *bilībaną. varda completely in the present tense, and partly in the past tense.

sv:blott.etymology: From blôt, from *blōt. blöt. Compare bloß, bloot, blot.

sv:blåsa.etymology: From blása, from *blēsaną. Cognate with blåsa, blåsa and blæse

sv:bocka.etymology: From bokka, bukka, from bucken, from *bukkōn, from *bukkōn.

sv:bort.etymology: From burt, brott, braut. See bryta for more.

sv:bra.etymology: Since at least 1621, from braf; from brav; from brave, borrowed from bravo.

sv:bryta.etymology: From bryta, from brjóta, from *breutaną, from *bʰrewd-.

sv:bråka.etymology: From brake, probably from or related to *brekan. Compare braak.

sv:budskap.etymology: From boðskapr. Akin to skap, like Botschaft.

sv:byta.etymology: From býta, from būten, of uncertain ultimate origin; possibly a - borrowing, from *boudi. If so, related to the name of Boudica, a British Celtic queen.

sv:börja.etymology: From byria, from byrja, from *burjaną. Derived from *bʰer-.

sv:del.etymology: From del, from dēl, deil, from dēl.

sv:dit.etymology: From þit, from þít, according to SAOB likely from þí + at. þí is in turn an old locative, possibly related to 𐌸𐌴𐌹, and more distantly to τεῖ in τεῖδε. Equivalent to ty + åt.

sv:draga.etymology: From dragha, from draga, from *draganą, from *dʰregʰ-. In some senses, from dragen (compare tragen).

sv:dryg.etymology: From drygher, from drjúgr, from *dreugaz. Cognate to друг.

sv:drömma.etymology: From drø̄ma, from dreyma, from *draumijaną. Cognate to dream, dromen and träumen.

sv:dum.etymology: From dumber, from dumbr, from *dumbaz, from *dʰewbʰ-. Compare dumb, dum, dumbur, dumb, dom and dumm.

sv:dygn.etymology: From dygn, dyghn, døgn, døghn, from dœgn, from *dōgin-, alternative form of *dōg-. mid-14th century.SO}} Cognate with døgn, døgn and døgn. See also dœgr, døger and dægur.

sv:därför.etymology: From þær for, equivalent to för. Compare therefore, derfor, dafür.

sv:dålig.etymology: From dáligr, compare with dårlig, dårlig, dåleg.

sv:egen.etymology: From eiginn, from *aiganaz, past participle of *aiganą. Equivalent to -en. Cognate with own.

sv:elak.etymology: From elaker, from e- + *laker (from Old Norse lakr, cognate with lack).

sv:emot.etymology: From i mot, equivalent to mot.

sv:ena.etymology: From ena. Cognate with ene, ene, eine, eina, einen. Equivalent to a.

sv:enkel.etymology: From enkil, from enkel, from *ainakulaz, equivalent to en + -el. Compare etymology of simple. Cognate with enkel, enkelt, enkel, ekkil, enkel and 𐌰𐌹𐌽𐌰𐌺𐌻𐍃. Compare also singulus with the same suffix. See also änka and änk

sv:enstaka.etymology: From -. staka, variant form of stake.

sv:entusiasm.etymology: Ultimately from ἐνθουσιασμός, from ἐν + θεός + οὐσία.

sv:erbjuda.etymology: From erbieten. Cognate with erbyde, erbiude, erbēden. Equivalent to bjuda.

sv:evig.etymology: ævigher, êwich; related to Old Norse ævi.

sv:fall.etymology: From fall, from falla. The grammatical sense is a calque of Latin casus.

sv:farlig.etymology: From fārliker, from varlik. Equivalent to lig.

sv:fast.etymology: From faster, from fastr, from *fastuz; see it for cognates and further etymology.

sv:fatta.etymology: vāten, from *fatōn, from *fatōn, from *fatōną. Cognate with fatte, fatte, vatten and fassen.

sv:fel.etymology: See Norwegian feil and Danish fejl. Used in Swedish at least since 1527. For the adverb, the now obsolete form felt was the dominant written form until the mid 19th century.

sv:finnas.etymology: From finnas, from finnask. Cognate with finnes and finnast.

sv:fler.etymology: From flere, flæster, from fleiri, from *flaizô, derived from *pleh₁-. Cognate, among others, with fleiri, flestr, plūs and πλέως, πλεῖστος.

sv:folk.etymology: From fōlk, from Runic Swedish fulk, from fólk, folk, from *fulką.

sv:fort.etymology: Attested since 1609 according to ''Nationalencyklopedins Ordbok'', from fôrt, which is used adverbially (forts) with the same meaning in Low German, from fort, from forth. Related to för, före and forsla.

sv:framställa.etymology: From ställa. Cognate with fremstille, fremstille, framstille, framstilla and framstille.

sv:framåt.etymology: From åt, also written as separate words, attested as such (''fram åt'') in the 1541 Swedish Bible translation (Ezekiel 1:12).

sv:frukta.etymology: From frukta, frokta, frykta, from vruchten, from forhtian, from *furhtijan.

sv:främst.etymology: From fram. Intuitively "forthest/forwardest," as in most forward.

sv:fråga.etymology: From vrāge (Frage), from *frāgu, from *frēgō. Compare frain. Displaced native spörja, spörsmål.

sv:fungera.etymology: From fungieren, from fungor,0250.html fungera from *bʰewg-. Cognate with fungere, fungere, fungera, fungere, fungeren, function, fungible, fungovat, fungovať, fungere, fungir, fonctionner.

sv:funka.etymology: From the ''funk-'' in funktion which is borrowed from function, from fonction, from functiōnem, accusative of functiō, from functus perfect participle of fungor. fungera, which is borrowed from fungor via fungieren.

sv:fästa.etymology: From fæsta, from festa, from *fastijaną, equivalent to -a. Cognate with fæste, feste, festa. Compare fasten.

sv:förankra.etymology: From verankern or verankeren, equivalent to ankra. Cognate with forankre, forankre and forankra, forankre.

sv:förföra.etymology: From vorvoren or verführen. Equivalent to föra.

sv:förkasta.etymology: From forkasta, equivalent to kasta. Cognate with forkaste, forkasta, forkaste, forkaste, forcast, forcasten. See also calques vorwerfen, verwerfen, verwerpen and forthrow with the same meaning.

sv:förklara.etymology: From forklara, from vorklaren,saob equivalent to -a or klara. Cognate with forklare, forklare, forklara, forklare, forklåra, forklåre, verklaren, verklaore, verklaar and erklären.

sv:förkunna.etymology: From forkynna, forkynda, forkunna, from vorkunden. Compare verkünden, forkynde.

sv:förlora.etymology: From vorloren (verloren), the past participle of vorlêsen, from farliosan, from *fraleusan, from *fraleusaną. förlisa. Compare verloor.

sv:förmå.etymology: From younger formā, apocopic form of older formāga, formāgha, from vermogen (or vermögen), equivalent to må. Cognate with formå, formå, formuga, younger fyrirmoga and vermogen.saob0261.html förmå

sv:förr.etymology: From fyr, from fyrr, from *furiz, comparative of *furi, *furai.

sv:förra.etymology: From fyrre, from fyrri, from *furizô, comparative of *furi, *furai.

sv:försiktig.etymology: ig, like German vorsichtig and Dutch ''voorzichtig''

sv:förstå.etymology: Through apocope with umlaut from forstanda, from vörstenden, from farstandan. Cognate with forstå. Equivalent to stå.

sv:förstås.etymology: The adverb has developed from a verb usage meaning "it is understood" (describing a statement).

sv:försvara.etymology: From forsvara, vorantworden (cf. verantworten and verantwoorden), equivalent to svara. Cognate with forsvare, forsvare, forsvara, forsvare.

sv:försäkra.etymology: From forsækra, from vorsekeren,saob equivalent of -a or säkra. Cognate with forsikre, forsikre, forsikre, forsikra, verzekeren and versichern.

sv:förvara.etymology: From forvara, from vorwaren. Cognate with forvare, forvare, forvare, forvara, verwaren and verwahren. Equivalent to vara.

sv:förändra.etymology: verändern, equivalent to ändra. Compare forandre.

sv:ganska.etymology: From gans, gansch, from ganz, from ganz, from *gant.

sv:genast.etymology: From genast, originally superlative of gen, as in "in the shortest time". Cognate of gainest.

sv:genomföra.etymology: From föra, probably after durchführen, whence also doorvoeren.

sv:gift.etymology: poison From Gift, from gift, gift, from *gifti, from *giftiz, which is a derivation of *gebaną.

sv:gilla.etymology: From gilda, from gilda. Compare gilda and gildr.

sv:glömma.etymology: gløma, from gleyma. Cognate with glemme, gløyma, gloyma.

sv:grann.etymology: pretty From grannr, with semantic shift "thin, fine" > "fine, pretty".

sv:gärna.etymology: From gjarna, from *gernô, the adverbial form of *gernaz.

sv:göra.etymology: From gøra, gæra, giora, from gera, gøra, gørva, from *garwijaną. Compare with yare and gear. * The noun is a nominalization of the verb. Literally "doing."

sv:handla.etymology: From handla, from handla, hǫndla, from *handlōną. In the sense ''trade'' influenced by from handelen and handeln.

sv:hav.etymology: From haf, from haf, from *habą, and ultimately from *kap-.

sv:hemlig.etymology: From hemeliker, from heimiligr, from heimelik, from *haimalīk, from *haimaz. Compare with homely.

sv:hemsk.etymology: hemsker, derived from hem. The original meaning was equivalent to homely, ergo "one who has only stayed at home" or "one who has not been out in the world", and subsequently "stupid" or "easily terrified". Cognate of hei

sv:hit.etymology: From - ''hit'', from *''hī''+''at''. * ''hī'', from *kei- (as in ἐκεῖ) * ''at'', from *at, from *ád (as in Swedish åt) Composed in a similar way: hegat and hingað. thumb|x270px|Pressing the button marked '''HIT''' (to he

sv:hitta.etymology: From hitta, from hitta, from *hittijaną, from *keyd-.

sv:hjälpa.etymology: From hiælpa, from hjalpa, from *helpaną, from *ḱelb-, *ḱelp-.

sv:hjälpsam.etymology: From sam. Compare UK dialectal helpsome.

sv:hopp.etymology: From hopp, from hōpen, from *hopon, from *hopōn.

sv:hoppa.etymology: From hoppa, huppa, from hoppa, from *huppōną, from *kewb-.

sv:hota.etymology: From hóta, derived from the noun hót (cf. hot). It has replaced an older (now obsolete) verb, höta, from hœta, from *hwōtijaną, cognate with høde, 𐍈𐍉𐍄𐌾𐌰𐌽.

sv:hov.etymology: From hōv, from hófr, from *hōfaz, from *ḱoph₂ós. Cognate with hov, hoof, Huf and hoef.

sv:hur.etymology: Shortened form of huru, from hwaru, from neuter dative of *hwar

sv:hylla.etymology: Related to hjälle, itself from hjallr. Cognate with hylle, hylde, hilla.

sv:häva.etymology: From hæfia, from hefja, from *habjaną, from *kh₂pyé-, from the root *kap-. Compare hæve, hevja, heave, heffen, heben. Doublet of hiva.

sv:hålla.etymology: From halda, halla, holda, holla, from halda, from *haldaną. Further etymology uncertain; possibly from *ḱel-.

sv:höger.etymology: From hǿgri, comparative of hǿgr, from *hōgiz. Cognate with hægri, højre and høyre.

sv:ifrågasätta.etymology: sätta, cognate with German in Frage stellen, used in Swedish since 1792.

sv:igång.etymology: gång, also written as separate words

sv:igår.etymology: From í gær, í gjár (whence í gær and í gjár). Akin to går.

sv:ihjäl.etymology: From Late ihiäl, from Early i hæl, from í hel (see hel, from *haljō), cognate with ihjel and i hel.

sv:ihåg.etymology: Compound of håg, literally "to one's mind".

sv:illa.etymology: From illa, from ílla, illa, adverb formation of ill, ilder, íllr, illr. Related to ill.

sv:ingenstans.etymology: From ænginstads, ingenstadz, jngen stedz. Equivalent to stans. Compare ingensteds, ingensteds.

sv:inställning.etymology: EinstellungSO or ing.SAOB Compare indstilling, innstilling, Einstellung, instelling.

sv:irrationell.etymology: From irratiōnālis. Cognate of irrationell, irrationel, irrational.

sv:iscensätta.etymology: sätta. Compare iscenesette, iscenesætte, in Szene setzen, mettre en scène.

sv:jaga.etymology: From iagha, from Early Old Swedish iagha, from jaga, from jāgen, from *jagōn, from *jagōn.

sv:jobba.etymology: Verbalization of jobb. Compare jobbe and jobba/jobbe.

sv:ju.etymology: From iū, io. Compare jo, jo, ja (adverb) / je (conjunction).

sv:kansli.etymology: Kanzlei, from cancelli. Cognate of chancellery, chancery.

sv:klocka.etymology: From klockæ, from klokka, from clocca, probably of - origin, from *klokkos (compare cloch, clog), from *klēg-, *klōg-.

sv:komma.etymology: From koma, from koma, from *kwemaną, from *gʷem-. orgasm is probably a come.

sv:kompis.etymology: kompanjon is. Compare Kumpel, kompel, kumpel, compa.

sv:konka.etymology: Short for konkursa, göra konkurs, similar to konka and konke.

sv:konstgjord.etymology: From gjord, past participle of göra.

sv:korrespondent.etymology: From Medieval Latin ''correspondens'', cognate with correspondent, Korrespondent. Used in Swedish since 1797.

sv:kraft.etymology: From krapter, from kraptr, krǫptr, from *kraftuz.

sv:krig.etymology: krîch. Unlike and krig, the Swedish word has neutrum gender like kríggj.

sv:kristen.etymology: From kristin, from kristinn, from kristen or cristen, from Christianus, from χρῑστιᾱνός.

sv:kritik.etymology: Borrowed from critique, from criticus, from κριτικός.

sv:kvinnlig.etymology: From qvinliker, qvinzliker, from kvennsligr and kvennligr. Akin to lig.

sv:kväll.etymology: From quæld, qvælder, from kveld, from *kwildiz, from *gʷelH-.

sv:kämpa.etymology: From kempe; see kamp. Compare kæmpe and kjempe

sv:kännas.etymology: Passive of känna. Literally, "to be felt."

sv:köpa.etymology: From køpa, from keypa, kaupa, from *kaupijaną, *kaupōną, from *kaupô, caupo, caupōnor. Cognate with købe, kjøpe, kaufen, kopen and cheap.

sv:köra.etymology: From køra, from keyra, from *kaurijaną, *karjaną. More at cair.

sv:laglig.etymology: lig, from lǫgligr. Cognate with löglegur.

sv:linje.etymology: From linia, from linea, from līnum, from *līno-.

sv:lite.etymology: Contraction of litet, neuter of liten. Compare mycket, with similar formation.

sv:lova.etymology: From lova, from lofa, from *lubōną, equivalent to -a. Cognate with love, love, loven, loben.

sv:lycka.etymology: lucke, gelucke. According to the OED, it may be related to the source of lock (compare *lūkaną). Compare and lykke, and lukke. Compare also luck, Glück, גליק, gelok, and geluk, and koloku.

sv:lycklig.etymology: lig. Similar to lykkelig and lukkeleg. Compare also גליקלעך and glücklich.

sv:lysa.etymology: From lȳsa, from lýsa. Compare dialectal ljusa, lyse.

sv:läge.etymology: Related to ligga and lägga, like German Lage.

sv:lära.etymology: From lēre, from lēra. Compare lære.

sv:läsa.etymology: From læsa, from lesa, from *lesaną, from *les-.

sv:låta.etymology: From lata, from láta, from *lētaną, from *leh₁d-. The sense “to sound” was also present in Old Norse and can be derived from the sense “to let (sound) go”.

sv:löpa.etymology: From løpa, from hlaupa, from *hlaupaną, from *klewb-.

sv:man.etymology: From maþer, mander, from maðr, from *mann-.

sv:mana.etymology: From manen, from manon, from *manōną, cognate with manian.

sv:mena.etymology: From mena, from mēnen, meinen (compare meina, mene), from mēnian, from *mainijaną, from *mein-.

sv:minnas.etymology: Reflexive or passive form of minna, from minna.

sv:mycken.etymology: From mikinn, accusative of mikill, from *mikilaz, from *meǵh₂-.

sv:mycket.etymology: Originally neuter singular of mycken, from mykin, mikin, accusative singular of mikil, from mikill, from *mikilaz, from *meǵh₂-.

sv:mysig.etymology: Attested since 1762. Derived from ''mysa'' ("to smile (slightly) with contentedness/comfort").''Svenska Akademiens ordbok'', column [https://web.archive.org/web/20160305023008/http://g3.spraakdata.gu.se/saob/show.phtml?f

sv:märklig.etymology: From mærkeliker, from merkiligr. Compare merkeleg, mærkelig and merkelig.

sv:måla.etymology: From mála. Cognate with mála and male, from mālen.

sv:måndag.etymology: From mānadagher, from mánadagr, from *mānini dag, a calque of dies lunae, equivalent of dag. Cognate with mandag, måndag, mandag, mánudagur, mánadagur, maanantai, Monday, Montag and maandag.

sv:mången.etymology: From manger, margher, marghin, from mangr, margr, from *managaz.

sv:mörk.etymology: From myrker, mørker, from myrkr, from *merkuz. Cognate with murk.

sv:ner.etymology: A contraction of earlier neder, from niðr, from *niþer, from *niter.

sv:nog.etymology: From nóg, nógr, gnógr, from *ganōgaz. Ultimately from *h₂eh₂nóḱe, perfective of *h₂neḱ-.

sv:noga.etymology: From nōgha, from nouwe. Compare genau.

sv:nämna.etymology: From næmna, from nefna, nemna, from *namnijaną, from *h₁nómn̥.

sv:när.etymology: From nær, from *nēhwiz, comparative of *nēhw. Ultimately from *h₂neḱ-.

sv:närma.etymology: From närmare, comparative of nära, likely influenced by nærme.

sv:nästa.etymology: From næstr, a superlative of ná, corresponding to *nēhwist.

sv:nå.etymology: From na, from ná. Ultimately from *h₂neḱ-.

sv:någon.etymology: From late naghan, from earlier nokon, accusative of nokor, from nǫkkurr, from - ''*ne-wait-ek-hwarjaʀ'' (literally, "not-know-I-who"). Cognate with nokon, nogen, nakar, nokkur, noen.

sv:någonsin.etymology: From sinn. Note that ''sinn'' is a neuter noun, and ''någon'' is thus the old neuter plural form. Compare någonting.

sv:nåt.etymology: From not, nut, from *hnōjaną, from *kneh₂-. Cognate with not, not, not, nót and Nut.not

sv:också.etymology: Corresponding to och / ock + så, from ok svā, from ok and svá. Compare også.

sv:oerhörd.etymology: From unerhört, negation of erhört, past participle of erhören. Equivalent to hörd.

sv:om.etymology: From um, from *umbi, from *h₂m̥bʰi. * As a conjunction, um superseded or blended with Old Norse ef and em, taking on their function as well. This is from *jabai, whence also if and ob. jäv, direct descendant of ef (see t

sv:omgång.etymology: From umganger, from umgangr, from *umbigangaz, equivalent to gång.

sv:omkring.etymology: From umkring, equivalent to om + kring.

sv:onsdag.etymology: From oþinsdagher, from óðinsdagr, from *Wōdanas dag.

sv:or.etymology: Related to orna, oret, of obscure ultimate origin. Compare oren.

sv:ordentlig.etymology: From ordentlich, from ordenlich (cognate with ordenlīcho), from orden, from ordō, from *ordō.

sv:oro.etymology: ro, the negation of ro, from -. Definition 3 is likely a direct loan from German Unruh.

sv:orolig.etymology: From rolig. Rolig, in the meaning ''calm'', is obsolete in contemporary Swedish so ''rolig'' is not considered an antonym of this word. (In contemporary Swedish, rolig means ''funny''.)

sv:orsaka.etymology: From orsaken, equivalent of -a. Cognate with årsage, forårsake, forårsake, forårsaka, orsaken, older oorzaken and older ursachen.saob

sv:person.etymology: From persona. the late 14th century. persona.

sv:podd.etymology: From pod or podcast, borrowed from podcast.

sv:prata.etymology: From praten, probably of sv origin. Compare prate and prattle, práta.

sv:rak.etymology: From rakr, related to rekja. Compare right.

sv:redo.etymology: From rēþo, probably from rēde, reide. Cognate with rede, reiður.

sv:rensa.etymology: From rensa, rænsa, from hreinsa, from *hrainisōną.

sv:riktig.etymology: From richtich or richtig. Compare rigtig.

sv:rimlig.etymology: -lig. Note that the verb rimma is not only used in the literal sense "to rhyme" but also in the figurative sense "to fit".

sv:ropa.etymology: From ropa, from hrópa, from *hrōpaną. Cognate with rópa, hrópa, råbe, rope.

sv:rättslig.etymology: From rætliker, equivalent to -lig. Compare rechtlich.

sv:råg.etymology: From rogher, from rugr, from *rugiz. Cognate with rug, rúgur, rogge, Roggen, and rye.

sv:råka.etymology: thumb|en råka (a rook) hrókr, from *hrōkaz, ultimately from *ker-; see rook#Etymology_1 for more.

sv:röd.etymology: From røþer, from rauðr, from *raudaz, from *h₁rowdʰós < *h₁rewdʰ-.

sv:röst.etymology: From raust, ultimately from a - derivative of *h₃reyH-.922 Related to *runsiz. Cognate with røst.

sv:sak.etymology: sǫk, from *sakō. Cognate with sak, sak, sag, sök, sake, zaak, Saak, Sook, Sache. An unrelated word that also underwent the transformation in meaning from "legal matter" to "thing, item" is causa.

sv:sanning.etymology: sannind, sannindi, from sannind. Cognate of sannindi.

sv:sedan.etymology: From siþan, from síðan. See Norwegian siden. Cognate with siþþan.

sv:sikte.etymology: From sikte, from sichte. Compare sikt.

sv:sjunde.etymology: From siundi, from sjaundi, from *sebundô. syvende, which was borrowed from Danish.

sv:skaffa.etymology: From skaffa, from schaffen, from scaffan (from scepfen, from *skappjan. Cognate with skepja (see skapa)).

sv:skandera.etymology: scandō, suffixed with -era. Cognate with skandieren, scander, scan.

sv:skapa.etymology: From skapa, from skapa, from *skapjaną. Related to German schaffen and English shape.

sv:ske.etymology: From ske, from schên, from skehan, from *skehan. Cognate with ske, skje, geschehen, geschieden, sji-jje.

sv:skepp.etymology: From skip, from skip, from *skipą. Sense 2 is a navis.

sv:skicka.etymology: From skikka, from schicken "to send" (schicken, schikken). Cognate with ske "to happen, to occur". Compare Trøndelag sjekk.

sv:skilja.etymology: From skilia, from skilja, from *skiljaną, from *(s)kelH-.

sv:skratta.etymology: a, used since 1561, cognate with skratte, related to an obsolete Swedish word ''skrata'' (to scare away by making noise).

sv:skrev.etymology: Used since 1752, cognate with skræv, possibly from Old High German ''gascrevŏn'' (to scratch, to cut), in the sense of a place of division.

sv:skri.etymology: skri, from or related to skríkja. Cognate with Schrei.

sv:skrika.etymology: From skríkja, from *skrīkijaną. Cognate to shriek/skrike and schreien.

sv:skriva.etymology: From skriva, from skrifa, from *skrībaną, a late borrowing from scrībō. Cognate with skrive, skriva, skrive, skrifa, skriuwe, shrive, schrieven, schrijven and schreiben.

sv:skuld.etymology: From skuld, from *skuldiz, from *(s)kéltis. Equivalent to skola.

sv:skyldig.etymology: ig, from skyldogher, skuldogher, from skuld, skull. In part influenced by schuldich and schuldig.

sv:skämt.etymology: From skæmt, from skæmta, whence also modern skämta. Cognate with skæmt, skjemt and skjemt.

sv:skär.etymology: pink chair, from the phrase couleur de chair.

sv:skön.etymology: From skön, from schö̂ne, from skōni, from *skaunī, from *skauniz, related to *skuþōną, which yielded skåda. Compare schön, sheen, skøn.

sv:sköt.etymology: Probably related to sköte, from skaut.

sv:sköta.etymology: From sköta, equivalent to -a. Compare skeyta, skjøtte.

sv:slippa.etymology: From slippa, from sleppa, from or related to *slīpaną.

sv:sluta.etymology: slūta, from sluten, from slūten, from *slūtan.

sv:slutsats.etymology: From sats. Cognate with slutsats, sluttsats, sluttsats, Schlusssatz, Schluss-Satz.

sv:släppa.etymology: From sleppa (past tense sleppti), from *slampijaną, from *(s)lembʰ-, see also *limpaną.

sv:snabb.etymology: Borrowed from the stem of snaben.807

sv:snäv.etymology: From snǣver, from snæfr. Compare snæver. Arguably related to snabb.

sv:som.etymology: From som or sum, in Runic inscriptions also ''sim'', same as sem, from sem. Also related to the prefix sam- and suffix -sam. Still in the Poetic Edda, the Icelandic ''sem'' is only used as a comparative particle, e.g. Há

sv:spel.etymology: From spil, from spil and spil, from *spil.

sv:spela.etymology: From spila, borrowed from spillen, from spilōn, from *spilōn. Equivalent to a.

sv:sprida.etymology: From spridha, probably the same word as spredha, from sprēden, spreiden, from *spraidijaną. Cognate with spread and spreiten. Due to the absence of this word in Old Icelandic, the Swedish word as well as sprede, spre, an

sv:spränga.etymology: From sprængia, from sprengja, from *sprangijaną, causative of *springaną. springa.

sv:stamp.etymology: From stamp, ultimately related to the verb stampa.

sv:stan.etymology: Contraction of staden, the definite singular of stad.

sv:stark.etymology: From starker, from starkr, from *starkuz, from *sterg-.

sv:steg.etymology: From stig. Cognate with steg, stig, stig.

sv:sticka.etymology: stikka, from *stikkô, from *(s)teyg-, related to Etymology 2 below. Compare stika, stick.

sv:stiga.etymology: From stigha, from stíga, from *stīganą. Cognate with stige, stige, sty, steigen, stijgen.

sv:stoppa.etymology: From stoppa, from stoppen, from *stoppon, from *stoppōn.

sv:stor.etymology: From stor, from stórr, from *stōraz, from *stāro-.

sv:storm.etymology: From stormber, from stormr, from *sturmaz, from *(s)twerH-.

sv:ställa.etymology: From stælla, from stellen, from stellian, from *stalljan.

sv:ställd.etymology: From the past participle of ställa.

sv:ställe.etymology: From stellen, from stellian. Cf Stelle.

sv:stämma.etymology: Borrowed from stemmen, from *stemnian, from *stabnijan, from *stabnijaną.

sv:ständig.etymology: ig, similar to German ständig. The Swedish/German verb stå/stehen is the basis for the noun stånd/Stand, which can mean both upright standing (without support) and still standing (without movement or change). The still-s

sv:stöd.etymology: From late Old Swedish stydh, from earlier stuþ, stoþ, from stoð, stuð, from *stuþs, from *stut-. Ultimately from *stew-.

sv:stödja.etymology: From Late stødhia, from styþia, from styðja, from *stuþjaną.

sv:support.etymology: From French (or German) and English support. Attested since 1697.

sv:svag.etymology: From swak, from *swak, from *swak. Compare with schwach. The form with -g- is due to - influence.

sv:svara.etymology: From svara, from *swarōną, cognate to answer. Compare svar.

sv:svart.etymology: From svarter, from svartr, from *swartaz, from *swordo-. Cognate with zwart, swart, schwarz, svartur and sort. Related to Latin sordes, sordere.

sv:sväva.etymology: From svæva‚ likely borrowed from swēven, from *swivian, from *swibāną. sviva.

sv:svår.etymology: From svār, svāger, svor, from svárr, from *swēraz, from *swer-. Compare schwer.

sv:syn.etymology: From syn, from sýn, sjón, from *siuniz.

sv:sämst.etymology: Cognate with sæmest, further etymology uncertain.

sv:särskild.etymology: Originally the past participle form of särskilja.

sv:sätta.etymology: From sætia, from setja, from *satjaną. Cognate with set.

sv:sådär.etymology: där, in sense 1 more often written as separate words

sv:tappa.etymology: From tapa. In the sense “to tap” from tappen.

sv:tidig.etymology: From tíðligr and tidelik, related to tid.

sv:tillbaka.etymology: From til baka, from til + baka, genitive plural of baker, equivalent to baks, according to SAOB online the alternative forms with -s are however not hence this fact, but rather from the genitive singular. Cognate with ti

sv:tillfällig.etymology: Partly from tōvallich, tōvellich from tōval + -ich and partly from ig. Cognate with, but with a different meaning than, tilfældig, tilfeldig, zufällig and toevallig.

sv:tillgänglig.etymology: sv. Cognate of zugänglich. Compare förgänglig, oundgänglig.

sv:tillsammans.etymology: From til saman, til samans, from tosamene. Cognate with tilsammen, til sammen, tilsammen, zusammen, tousommen, tosamen, tezamen and zesummen.

sv:timme.etymology: From time, from tími, from *tīmô, from *tī-, from *dī-.

sv:titta.etymology: Probably sv child-speak, similar to titte.

sv:tjäna.etymology: From þiǣna, þiāna, þiēna, from þjóna, þéna. Akin to dienen.

sv:total.etymology: From total, from total, from tōtālis.

sv:tott.etymology: From þáttr, from *þanhtu-, from *tonk-tu-.533 According to Pokorny, this is related to *teḱ-, see also texō, dūhen.

sv:trappa.etymology: From trapa, trappa, borrowed from trappe, from *trappa, from *trappā. Similar to trapp, trappe and trappa.

sv:tre.etymology: From þrir, þrī, from Runic Swedish þrīR, from þrír, from ᚦᚱᛁᛃᛟᛉ, from *þrīz, ultimately from *tréyes. Compare Norwegian and Danish tre, Icelandic þrír, Faroese tríggir.

sv:trovärdig.etymology: From värdig, compare with troverdig and truverdig.

sv:tvinga.etymology: From þvinga, from þvinga, from *þwinganą, from *þwangiz. Cognates: see zwingen.

sv:tvärtom.etymology: From om. Perhaps from notion of a quick about-turn.

sv:två.etymology: From tver, from tveir, from *twai, from *dwóh₁.

sv:tycka.etymology: From þykkia, þykia, from þykkja, from *þunkijaną.

sv:udda.etymology: From oddi, dative singular of oddr.

sv:underbar.etymology: wunderbar, equivalent to -bar. Compare and underbar, wonderbaar, wunderbar and wunnerbor.

sv:upprepa.etymology: From earlier uppreppa, from upreppa, from upreppen.

sv:utdragen.etymology: dragen, compare drawn out. Attested since 1835.

sv:utgång.etymology: From ūtganger, from útgangr, from *ūtgangaz. Equivalent to gång.

sv:utländsk.etymology: From utlændsker, utlænzker. Compare ausländisch and outlandish.

sv:utplåna.etymology: plåna, literally to (wipe) out from a slate

sv:utropa.etymology: Compound of ropa, compare ropa ut.

sv:uttala.etymology: From tala. Compare udtale, uttale and uttala.

sv:vakna.etymology: From vakna, from vakna, from *waknaną, from *weǵ-.

sv:vanlig.etymology: vanaligr. Compare vanlig, vanalegur and vanleg.

sv:vara.etymology: vara, væra from vera, earlier vesa, from *wesaną. Cognate with være, vera, være.

sv:vart.etymology: From hvart, shortened form of var-åt, "towards where".

sv:vass.etymology: From hvas, from hvǫss, hvass, from *hwassaz, from *kʷh₁dstós.

sv:vecka.etymology: From vika, from vika, from *wikǭ, from *weyg-.

sv:verka.etymology: From värkia, from verka, from *werką, from *wérǵom. Compare werken and wirken.

sv:veta.etymology: From vita, from vita, from *witaną, ultimately from *weyd-.

sv:vetta.etymology: From vita, ''vet(t)a'', from vita, from *witaną, ultimately from *weyd-. veta.

sv:vi.etymology: From vir, from *wīʀ (compare vér), from *wīz, from *wéy, plural of *éǵh₂.

sv:viss.etymology: From viss, from *gawissaz. Cognate with viss.

sv:vit.etymology: From hviter, from hvítr, from *hwītaz, ultimately from *ḱweytos.

sv:vittna.etymology: From vitna, from the corresponding noun to vittne.

sv:väcka.etymology: From vækia, vækkia, from vekja, from *wakjaną.

sv:väl.etymology: From vel, from *wela, from *welh₁-. Common Germanic word. Cognate with vel, wel, well, væl, wohl, 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐌻𐌰, vel, vel, vel.

sv:väldig.etymology: weldich, whence also vældig and veldig (which are usually used in a different way from the Swedish word). See the related gewaltig for more.

sv:välja.etymology: From vælia, from velja, from *waljaną. Causative of *wiljaną (see vilja).

sv:välkomna.etymology: The verb is derived from the adjective a

sv:välvillig.etymology: benevolus. Equivalent to villig. Compare velvillig.

sv:värd.etymology: From værþer from verðr, verð, from *werþaz, used substantively as a noun. Cognate with waard, wert, Wert, worth.

sv:värld.etymology: From væruld, værald, værild, værld, from verǫld, from *weraldiz. In (intensifier), perhaps elliptical for "världens största" (the world's largest) or the like.

sv:växa.etymology: From væxa, from vaxa, from *wahsijaną, from *h₂weg-, cognate with wax (of the moon).

sv:våga.etymology: From vagha, from vága, from wagen.

sv:äga.etymology: From ægha, from eiga, from *aigǭ, from *eik-.

sv:ägna.etymology: From eigna, related to eiginn. Related to äga and egen. Also compare eignen, own.

sv:älska.etymology: From ælska, from ælska (Compare elska). Ultimately from *aliskōną.

sv:ändå.etymology: From då. Compare endå, enda, endda, enda.

sv:ärlig.etymology: From ǣrlīker, from êrlich, from *aiʀulīk, equivalent to -lig. Cognate of ehrlich.

sv:även.etymology: From even, effen, from evan, from *ebn, from *ebnaz, cognate with even, even. Compare effen. See also jämn.

sv:åka.etymology: From aka, from aka, from *akaną. Cognate with age. Ultimately from *h₂eǵ-. Doublet of agera, which was borrowed from agō, from the same ultimate Proto-Indo-European source.

sv:ånga.etymology: The oblique case of ''ånge'' (in Early Modern Swedish), from ange. Compare ang and anga. Beyond the Nordic languages the origin is unclear, perhaps from *h₂enh₁-.

sv:ångra.etymology: From angra, from angra, equivalent to -a. Compare angre, angre, anger.

sv:år.etymology: From ar, from ár, from *jērą, from *yeh₁r-.

sv:åtminstone.etymology: From at minsto, + the feminine dative singular definite suffix definite ''-unni/-onne''. Equivalent to åt + dative form of modern minsta.

sv:öka.etymology: From øka, from auka, from *aukaną, from *h₂ewg-. Akin to eke, øge, 𐌰𐌿𐌺𐌰𐌽, augeō.

sv:ökänd.etymology: From ø̄dhkænder‚ from auðkendr, from kenna. Cognate with åkjendt, audkjend and auðkenndur.

sv:önska.etymology: From yskia, øskia, from œskja, from *wunskijaną. The 'n' stems from influence from Middle Low German wunschen. Compare wünschen.

sv:över.etymology: From ivir, yvir, ø̄wer, from Runic Swedish ufiR, from yfir, from *ubiri, from *upéri, from *upér, from *upo.

sv:överens.etymology: From ower ens, over en, equivalent of ens.

sv:överhuvudtaget.etymology: taget, from ovir hovudh. Likely borrowed from German, compare überhaupt.

sv:överleva.etymology: From leva. Calque of Latin supervivire.

sv:överraska.etymology: überraschen, equivalent to raska. Cognate of overraske.
